e: Bilateral sacroiliitis + marginal syndesmophytes (bamboo spine) = ankylosing spondylitis.

Snowman/figure-of-8 heart = supracardiac TAPVC.
Boot-shaped = TOF; egg-on-side = TGA.

Valvulae conniventes cross the entire lumen in jejunum.
Ileum is featureless; colonic haustra don't cross the full width.
Scurvy: child c̅ limb pain; X-ray shows Wimberger ring, Frankel's white line, Trümmerfeld zone, subperiosteal haemorrhage.

Putty kidney: dense, homogeneous, putty-like calcification of end-stage TB kidney (autonephrectomy).
Nephrocalcinosis = pyramidal/cortical calcification.

Neurons (non-dividing) are most radioresistant (Bergonié–Tribondeau law).
Marrow, spermatogonia, gut crypt cells are highly radiosensitive.
eFAST = rapid bedside first imaging in blunt trauma (haemo/pneumothorax, haemopericardium, intra-abdominal fluid).
GCT: eccentric lytic epiphyseal–metaphyseal lesion c̅ soft-tissue swelling (soap-bubble); classic at distal radius.
Ring-enhancing lesion in temporal lobe = temporal lobe abscess (commonly otogenic spread).

Combined hysteroscopy + laparoscopy = gold standard to confirm and classify Müllerian anomalies.
USG/HSG only screen.
Bilateral symmetric sacroiliac erosions + sclerosis = ankylosing spondylitis (sacroiliitis).

Turner syndrome (45,X): streak ovaries c̅ small uterus on USG.
Renal anomaly is horseshoe kidney, not single kidney.
Rigler's triad: small bowel obstruction + pneumobilia (air in biliary tree) + ectopic gallstone = gallstone ileus.

Suspected aortic dissection in an unstable patient → TEE (bedside, rapid, accurate).
CT angiography if stable.
Acute pancreatitis (bulky pancreas c̅ fluid): serum lipase ↑ (more specific, stays ↑ longer than amylase).
Renal trauma c̅ haematuria: contrast CT (c̅ delayed phase) is the investigation of choice to grade injury and localise bleeding.
Crescentic free gas under diaphragm on erect CXR = pneumoperitoneum → hollow viscus perforation.

Round metallic object (coin) behind the tracheal air column on lateral view = oesophagus.
Tracheal coins lie sagittally on AP.
Psoas major: paired muscle along anterolateral lumbar vertebral bodies on axial CT.

Cephalhematoma: subperiosteal, present since birth, limited by suture lines.
Caput succedaneum and subgaleal haematoma cross sutures.
Putty kidney (renal TB): dense, coarse, amorphous calcification c̅ sterile pyuria.

Inverse square law: intensity ∝ 1/d².
Rapidly dividing cells and small bowel mucosa are radiosensitive, not resistant.
RML consolidation: fever, cough, crepitations; loss of right heart border (silhouette sign).

IVU: contrast injected IV to opacify kidneys, ureters and bladder → invasive.
Gold standard for bladder cancer is cystoscopy.
Bird's beak oesophagus (achalasia): manometry = confirmatory test (↑ LES pressure, incomplete relaxation, aperistalsis).
RUL collapse: volume loss, upward displacement of horizontal fissure, ↑ opacity.
MRI of SI joints (STIR) shows active sacroiliitis/marrow oedema before X-ray changes → earliest modality.
